# claudebox v2 protocol (Nxeon fork)

This document describes the `/v2/*` API that the Nxeon `app` uses to drive Claude Code inside
the `claudebox` container. The original `/prompt`, `/health` and `/v1/*` (OpenAI compat) endpoints
are unchanged.

Verified against **Claude Code 2.1.287** (`claude --help`, real `claude -p` output and the
`sdk-tools.d.ts` shipped in the npm package).

## Authentication

Every `/v2/*` request needs `Authorization: Bearer $CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY`.
If `CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY` is unset, `/v2/*` returns 401 for everything (fail closed) unless
`CLAUDEBOX_ALLOW_NO_AUTH=1`. `/health` is unauthenticated.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| GET  | `/health` | `{status, activeRequests, version, claudeVersion, authMode, activeRuns, queuedRuns, maxConcurrent, firewallMode, autoPermissionMode}`. `authMode` is `oauth` \| `api_key` \| `credentials` \| `none`. |
| POST | `/v2/run` | Start a run; the response **is** the SSE stream (see below). |
| GET  | `/v2/run/:runId/events?fromSeq=N` | SSE: replay buffered events with `seq >= N` (inclusive, default 1), then follow live. Also honours the standard `Last-Event-ID` header (resumes at `id+1`) when `fromSeq` is absent. Ends immediately after replay if the run is finished. 404 if the run is unknown/expired. |
| GET  | `/v2/run/:runId` (alias `/v2/runs/:runId`) | Run info JSON (see `GET /v2/runs`). |
| POST | `/v2/abort` | `{runId}` → kills the run's whole process group (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 4 s). Queued runs are just dequeued. → `{ok, runId, found, status}` (`status: "aborting"` for a running run). 404 if unknown. |
| GET  | `/v2/runs` | `{runs:[RunInfo], running, queued, retained, maxConcurrent}` — active (queued + running) runs. `?all=1` includes finished runs still retained. |
| POST | `/v2/preview/start` | `{projectSlug, port, command?}` → PreviewStatus (200) / 400 / 409 (port busy) / 422 (cannot detect a command). |
| POST | `/v2/preview/stop` | `{projectSlug, port?}` → `{stopped, ...PreviewStatus}`. Also kills any *unmanaged* process listening on the port (e.g. a dev server Claude started via Bash), except running Claude runs. |
| GET  | `/v2/preview/status?projectSlug=&port=` | PreviewStatus. `port` optional (defaults to the managed port). |
| GET  | `/v2/previews` | `{previews:[PreviewStatus]}` |

`RunInfo = {runId, projectSlug, status: queued|running|done|error|aborted, mode, model, sessionId, pid, createdAt, startedAt, endedAt, exitCode, lastSeq, firstSeq, subscribers}` (times are epoch ms).

`PreviewStatus = {projectSlug, running, managed, listening, port, pid, kind: "process"|"static"|null, command, startedAt, exitCode, logTail: string[] (≤200 lines)}`.
`running = managed || listening` — `listening` comes from a TCP connect probe to `127.0.0.1:<port>` (and `::1`),
so a server Claude started itself is reported as running (with `managed: false`).

Errors are JSON `{error: "message"}` with an appropriate status.

### POST /v2/run body

```json
{
  "runId": "uuid (optional; generated if absent)  ^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}$",
  "prompt": "string",
  "projectSlug": "my-app",              // ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,47}$ ; cwd = $PROJECTS_DIR/<slug> (created if missing)
  "sessionId": "claude session id | null",   // → --resume
  "model": "opus|sonnet|haiku|<full id>",    // → --model
  "mode": "auto|edit|plan|ask",              // default auto
  "thinking": "off|normal|max",              // → env MAX_THINKING_TOKENS 0 / 8000 / 32000 (unset = CLI default)
  "effort": "low|medium|high|xhigh|max",     // optional → --effort
  "attachments": ["/workspace/uploads/<id>/<file>"],
  "appendSystemPrompt": "string",            // → --append-system-prompt
  "maxTurns": 50,                            // → --max-turns
  "previewPort": 4123,                       // 4100-4199 → env PORT/HOST/BASE_PATH for Claude's shell
  "authToken": "optional per-run token",
  "autocompactTokens": 80000,                // optional; 0/absent = CLI default ("auto"). See below.
  "agents": {"code-reviewer": {"description": "…", "prompt": "…", "tools": ["Read","Grep"], "model": "sonnet"}},
  "agent": "code-reviewer"                   // optional lead agent (must be a key of `agents` when given)
}
```

* `autocompactTokens` is the context size (tokens) at which auto-compaction fires. The CLI's
  `--autocompact` takes a *window* (100k–1M) and compacts at `window − 13k`, so claudebox passes
  `--autocompact <tokens+13000>`; below 87k it passes `--autocompact 100000` plus
  `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=<tokens/1000>` (percent of the 100k window → threshold = tokens).
  The model's own context window still caps it. Valid: 0 or 10 000–987 000.
* `agents` → `--agents <json>` (custom subagents; keys `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,47}$`, value
  `{description, prompt, tools?: string[] (omit = inherit all), model?: alias|full id|"inherit"}`).
  JSON larger than 32 KiB is written to a temp file (`--agents <path>`, allowed with `-p`) that is
  deleted when the run ends. In `edit` mode the `Agent` tool is added to `--allowedTools` when agents are passed.
* `agent` → `--agent <name>`: runs the main session *as* that agent (its prompt/tools/model).
* `--forward-subagent-text` is always passed when the CLI supports it (`FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT=0` disables):
  subagent text/thinking is forwarded as `text`/`thinking` events **tagged with `parentId`** (never merged
  into the main answer, no `block_end`).
* Manual compaction: send the prompt `/compact [instructions]` with `sessionId` (→ `--resume`).

* Attachments must resolve inside `$UPLOADS_DIR` or the project dir; each is appended to the
  prompt as `[Attached file: <path> — use Read tool]`. `--add-dir $UPLOADS_DIR` is always passed so
  Read works in every mode.
* `authToken` overrides the container env for that run: tokens starting with `sk-ant-api` are set
  as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` removed); anything else (e.g. `sk-ant-oat01-…`
  from `claude setup-token`) is set as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` removed).
* Child env: `CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY` and the server's `PORT` are removed. With `previewPort`:
  `PORT=<previewPort> HOST=0.0.0.0 BASE_PATH=/preview/<slug>/ NXEON_PREVIEW_PORT=<port>`.
  Always: `NXEON_PROJECT_SLUG`, `NXEON_RUN_ID`.
* Errors: 400 validation, 401 auth, 409 duplicate `runId` (use the events endpoint to reattach).
* Concurrency: at most `MAX_CONCURRENT` (default 4) runs execute; further runs wait silently in a
  FIFO queue (the SSE stream is open but emits nothing until the run starts; status `queued`).
* **Client disconnect never kills a run.** Only `/v2/abort` does. Reattach with
  `GET /v2/run/:runId/events?fromSeq=<lastSeenSeq+1>`. Event buffers (≤50 000 events per run) are kept
  for 30 minutes after completion (`RUN_RETENTION_MS`).

## CLI invocation

```
claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages \
       --permission-prompts none \
       [--model M] [--resume SID] [--max-turns N] [--effort E] [--append-system-prompt S] \
       --add-dir $UPLOADS_DIR [--autocompact W] [--agents JSON|FILE] [--agent NAME] [--forward-subagent-text] \
       <mode flags>  -- "<prompt>"
```

`stdin` is `/dev/null`; the child is spawned `detached` (own process group = pid) so abort can
kill the whole tree. `--permission-prompts none` (auto-deny anything that would prompt) is only passed when
the installed CLI advertises it in `--help` (feature detection at startup).

### Mode mapping (verified against `claude --help` of 2.1.287)

| mode | flags | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `auto` | `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` | Full tools. CLI 2.1.287 *does* have a `--permission-mode auto` (classifier-based), but it is gated per plan/model ("auto mode is unavailable for your plan/model") and can block actions when the classifier has no verdict — not reliable headless. Set `AUTO_PERMISSION_MODE=auto` to opt in. |
| `edit` | `--permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Read Edit Write Glob Grep Bash WebFetch WebSearch TodoWrite NotebookEdit TaskCreate TaskUpdate TaskGet TaskList [Agent]` | `Agent` only when custom `agents` are passed. Anything else (e.g. MCP) is auto-denied. |
| `plan` | `--permission-mode plan` | Read-only exploration. The plan arrives as an `ExitPlanMode` `tool_use` (`input.plan`); its approval is auto-denied, so the run then ends. |
| `ask` | `--permission-mode dontAsk --tools Read,Glob,Grep,WebFetch,WebSearch,TodoWrite,TaskCreate,TaskUpdate,TaskGet,TaskList --allowedTools <same>` | `--tools` removes Bash/Edit/Write from the model entirely; `dontAsk` denies anything not pre-approved. |

Thinking: `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS` = `0` (off) / `8000` (normal) / `32000` (max). On adaptive-thinking
models the CLI treats `0` as "thinking off"; non-zero values act as a budget.

Note: Claude Code ≥ 2.1 in `-p` mode uses **TaskCreate / TaskUpdate / TaskList** instead of TodoWrite.
Both are mapped to `todo` events.

## SSE format

```
id: <seq>
event: <type>
data: <json>

```

* `seq` starts at 1 per run and increases by 1; it is only in the `id:` line (not inside `data`).
* First frame is `retry: 2000`. Heartbeat comments (`: ping <ts>`) every 15 s.
* Response headers: `Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`, `X-Run-Id`, `X-Run-Status`,
  `X-Accel-Buffering: no`.
* The stream is closed by the server right after `done`.
* `done` is **always** the last event of a run (also for spawn failures, crashes and aborts).

### Normalized events (see `server/src/shared/protocol.ts`)

Extra fields beyond the protocol are additive and may be ignored.

| type | data |
|---|---|
| `init` | `{sessionId, model, tools[], cwd, permissionMode, claudeCodeVersion}` |
| `thinking` | `{delta, parentId?}` — `parentId` = forwarded subagent thinking (full block, no `block_end`) |
| `text` | `{delta, parentId?}` — `parentId` = forwarded subagent text (full block, no `block_end`) |
| `block_end` | `{kind: "thinking"\|"text"}` |
| `tool_use` | `{id, name, input, parentId?}` |
| `tool_result` | `{id, isError, content, parentId?}` — content stringified, truncated to 20 KiB (`…[truncated N bytes]`) |
| `todo` | `{todos:[{content, status, activeForm?, id?}]}` — full list each time |

# Nxeon Workspace — production stack (see SPEC.md §2)
#
#   Browser ─TLS─> Caddy (host :443) ─> 127.0.0.1:8080 ─> app ─> claudebox:3000 / :4100-4199
#                                                           └──> whisper:9000
#
# Only `app` is published, and only on host loopback (127.0.0.1:8080). Docker
# port publishing bypasses ufw, so nothing else may ever get a `ports:` entry.
#
# TRUST_PROXY: Caddy runs on the host and connects to 127.0.0.1:8080; docker-proxy
# forwards that into the `nxeon` network, so the app sees the peer address as the
# bridge GATEWAY (172.28.0.1), never 127.0.0.1. The subnet is pinned below so this
# value is deterministic. Only that single address is trusted to set X-Forwarded-For
# (claudebox/whisper live on the same subnet but must not be able to spoof it).
#
# Usage: deploy/up.sh   (or: sudo docker compose up -d --build)

name: nxeon

x-logging: &logging
  driver: json-file
  options:
    max-size: "10m"
    max-file: "3"

services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.app
    image: nxeon/app:latest
    container_name: nxeon-app
    restart: unless-stopped
    init: true
    env_file:
      - path: .env
        required: true
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      PORT: "8080"
      HOST: 0.0.0.0
      CLAUDEBOX_URL: http://claudebox:3000
      WHISPER_URL: http://whisper:9000
      PROJECTS_DIR: /data/projects
      UPLOADS_DIR: /data/uploads
      DB_PATH: /data/db/nxeon.db
      CLAUDEBOX_PROJECTS_DIR: /workspace/projects
      CLAUDEBOX_UPLOADS_DIR: /workspace/uploads
      TRUST_PROXY: 172.28.0.1/32
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./data/projects:/data/projects
      - ./data/uploads:/data/uploads
      - ./data/db:/data/db
    depends_on:
      claudebox:
        condition: service_started
      whisper:
        condition: service_started
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/health').then(r=>process.exit(r.ok?0:1)).catch(()=>process.exit(1))"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      start_period: 30s
      retries: 3
    mem_limit: 1g
    pids_limit: 512
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    logging: *logging
    networks:
      nxeon:
        ipv4_address: 172.28.0.10

  claudebox:
    build:
      context: ./claudebox
    image: nxeon/claudebox:latest
    container_name: nxeon-claudebox
    restart: unless-stopped
    # NOT published to the host: reachable only from `app` over the nxeon network
    # (API :3000, preview servers :4100-4199).
    expose:
      - "3000"
      - "4100-4199"
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN   # entrypoint installs the egress firewall, then drops the cap
      - NET_RAW
    environment:
      PORT: "3000"
      FIREWALL_MODE: open
      MAX_CONCURRENT: "4"
      PROJECTS_DIR: /workspace/projects
      UPLOADS_DIR: /workspace/uploads
      PREVIEW_PORT_MIN: "4100"
      PREVIEW_PORT_MAX: "4199"
      # Secrets come from .env (empty values = not set):
      CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY: ${CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY:?CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY must be set in .env}
      CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN:-}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}
    volumes:
      - ./data/projects:/workspace/projects
      - ./data/uploads:/workspace/uploads:ro
      - ./data/claude-home:/home/claude/.claude
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:3000/health >/dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      start_period: 30s
      retries: 3
    mem_limit: 4g
    memswap_limit: 5g
    pids_limit: 4096
    shm_size: 256m
    logging: *logging
    networks:
      nxeon:
        ipv4_address: 172.28.0.20

  whisper:
    build:
      context: ./whisper
    image: nxeon/whisper:latest
    container_name: nxeon-whisper
    restart: unless-stopped
    init: false   # image already runs tini as PID 1
    expose:
      - "9000"
    environment:
      WHISPER_MODEL: base        # base ≈ 2 s per 10 s clip on this VPS; "small" is more accurate but ~3.5x slower
      WHISPER_THREADS: "4"
      WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE: int8
      MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES: "26214400"
      MAX_AUDIO_SECONDS: "300"
      HF_HUB_OFFLINE: "1"
    volumes:
      - ./data/whisper-models:/models
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request,sys; sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:9000/health',timeout=4).status==200 else 1)"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      start_period: 60s
      retries: 3
    mem_limit: 1536m
    pids_limit: 256
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp:size=128m
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    logging: *logging
    networks:
      nxeon:
        ipv4_address: 172.28.0.30

networks:
  nxeon:
    name: nxeon
    driver: bridge
    driver_opts:
      com.docker.network.bridge.name: br-nxeon
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 172.28.0.0/24
          gateway: 172.28.0.1

# Claude context

Sample md file for Claude context inside agent container.
# Nxeon fork of claudebox (https://github.com/ArmanJR/claudebox, MIT)
FROM node:22-bookworm

# "latest" by default; override with --build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.287
ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=latest

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Dev tooling so Claude can "set up applications", plus firewall/init tooling.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
      git python3 python3-pip python3-venv build-essential ripgrep jq curl \
      ca-certificates procps iptables iproute2 dnsutils sudo tini less \
      unzip zip openssh-client util-linux && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Reuse uid/gid 1000: rename the node image's `node` user/group to `claude`.
RUN groupmod -n claude node && \
    usermod -l claude -d /home/claude -m -s /bin/bash node && \
    mkdir -p /home/claude/.claude /home/claude/.npm-global && \
    chown -R claude:claude /home/claude && \
    echo "claude ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL" > /etc/sudoers.d/claude && \
    chmod 0440 /etc/sudoers.d/claude

# Claude Code CLI
RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION} && \
    claude --version && \
    npm cache clean --force

ENV HOME=/home/claude \
    CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/home/claude/.claude \
    DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 \
    NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX=/home/claude/.npm-global \
    PATH=/home/claude/.npm-global/bin:/home/claude/.local/bin:$PATH \
    PIP_BREAK_SYSTEM_PACKAGES=1 \
    PROJECTS_DIR=/workspace/projects \
    UPLOADS_DIR=/workspace/uploads \
    FIREWALL_MODE=open

COPY entrypoint.sh /entrypoint.sh
COPY allowed-domains.txt /etc/allowed-domains.txt
COPY package.json server.js /opt/claudebox/
COPY lib /opt/claudebox/lib
RUN chmod 755 /entrypoint.sh && \
    mkdir -p /workspace/projects /workspace/uploads /workspace/.tmp && \
    chown -R claude:claude /workspace

WORKDIR /workspace

EXPOSE 3000 4100-4199

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=20s --retries=3 \
  CMD curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:${PORT:-3000}/health >/dev/null || exit 1

# tini is PID 1 (reaps orphaned dev servers). The entrypoint runs as root to
# install the firewall, then drops to the `claude` user (uid 1000) with
# NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW removed from the bounding set, so even `sudo` inside the
# container cannot alter the firewall.
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/tini", "-g", "--", "/bin/bash", "/entrypoint.sh"]
CMD ["node", "/opt/claudebox/server.js"]

Usage: claude [options] [command] [prompt]

Claude Code - starts an interactive session by default, use -p/--print for
non-interactive output

Arguments:
  prompt                                Your prompt

Options:
  --add-dir <directories...>            Additional directories to allow tool
                                        access to
  --agent <agent>                       Agent for the current session. Overrides
                                        the 'agent' setting.
  --agents <json-or-file>               JSON object defining custom agents, or
                                        with --print the path to a file that
                                        holds one (e.g. '{"reviewer":
                                        {"description": "Reviews code",
                                        "prompt": "You are a code reviewer"}}')
  --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions  Enable bypassing all permission checks
                                        as an option, without it being enabled
                                        by default. Recommended only for
                                        sandboxes with no internet access.
  --allowedTools, --allowed-tools <tools...>
      Comma or space-separated list of tool names to allow (e.g. "Bash(git *)
      Edit")
  --append-system-prompt <prompt>       Append a system prompt to the default
                                        system prompt
  --autocompact <auto|tokens>           Auto-compact window size (auto, or
                                        100k–1M tokens)
  --ax-screen-reader                    Render screen-reader friendly output
                                        (flat text, no decorative borders or
                                        animations).
  --bg, --background                    Start the session in the background and
                                        return immediately. Prints the id that
                                        `claude attach`, `logs`, `stop` and `rm`
                                        take; `claude agents` lists them. With
                                        --resume <session-id>, continues that
                                        session in the background under the same
                                        ID, or starts a copy and says so when
                                        the session is already running
  --bare                                Minimal mode: skip hooks (those defined
                                        in settings and by installed plugins;
                                        features built into Claude Code are
                                        unaffected), LSP, plugin sync,
                                        attribution, auto-memory, background
                                        prefetches, keychain reads, and
                                        CLAUDE.md auto-discovery. Sets
                                        CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1. Anthropic auth is
                                        strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or
                                        apiKeyHelper via --settings (OAuth and
                                        keychain are never read). 3P providers
                                        (Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry) use their own
                                        credentials. Skills still resolve via
                                        /skill-name. Explicitly provide context
                                        via: --system-prompt[-file],
                                        --append-system-prompt[-file], --add-dir
                                        (CLAUDE.md dirs), --mcp-config,
                                        --settings, --agents, --plugin-dir.
  --betas <betas...>                    Beta headers to include in API requests
                                        (API key users only)
  --brief                               Enable SendUserMessage tool for
                                        agent-to-user communication
  --chrome                              Enable Claude in Chrome integration
  --cloud [description|session_id|url]  Create a cloud session with the given
                                        description, or attach to an existing
                                        one by session ID or claude.ai/code URL
  -c, --continue                        Continue the most recent conversation in
                                        the current directory
  --dangerously-skip-permissions        Bypass all permission checks.
                                        Recommended only for sandboxes with no
                                        internet access.
  -d, --debug [filter]                  Enable debug mode with optional category
                                        filtering (e.g., "api,hooks" or
                                        "!1p,!file")
  --debug-file <path>                   Write debug logs to a specific file path
                                        (implicitly enables debug mode)
  --desktop                             Open in the Claude Desktop app instead
                                        of the terminal (with --continue or
                                        --resume <id> to pick the session)
  --disable-slash-commands              Disable all skills
  --disallowedTools, --disallowed-tools <tools...>
      Comma or space-separated list of tool names to deny (e.g. "Bash(git *)
      Edit")
  --effort <level>                      Effort level for the current session
                                        (low, medium, high, xhigh, max)
  --environment <environment_id>        Create a new cloud session that runs on
                                        the given self-hosted environment
                                        (ccpool_...).
  --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections
      Move per-machine sections (cwd, env info, memory paths, git status) from
      the system prompt into the first user message. Improves cross-user
      prompt-cache reuse. Only applies with the default system prompt (ignored
      with --system-prompt). (default: false)
  --fallback-model <model>              Enable automatic fallback to specified
                                        model(s) when the default model is

                                        order. Re-tries the primary at the start

                                        instead of reusing the original (use

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

# Skills Repository Overview

## Repository Structure

The repository is organized into the following main directories:

- **`./skills`** - Skill examples organized by category (Creative & Design, Development & Technical, Enterprise & Communication, and Document Skills)
- **`./spec`** - The Agent Skills specification
- **`./template`** - Skill template for creating new skills

## Licensing

### Open Source (Apache 2.0)
- Most example skills in the repository

### Source-Available (Proprietary)
- `skills/docx` - Document creation & editing for DOCX files
- `skills/pdf` - Document creation & editing for PDF files
- `skills/pptx` - Document creation & editing for PPTX files
- `skills/xlsx` - Document creation & editing for XLSX files

These source-available skills power Claude's document capabilities and are provided as reference implementations for complex, production-grade skills.

## Skill Format

All skills follow a simple, standardized format:

```markdown
---
name: my-skill-name
description: A clear description of what this skill does and when to use it
---

# My Skill Name

[Add your instructions here that Claude will follow when this skill is active]

## Examples
- Example usage 1
- Example usage 2

## Guidelines
- Guideline 1
- Guideline 2
```

**Required YAML frontmatter fields:**
- `name` - Unique identifier (lowercase, hyphens for spaces)
- `description` - Complete description of what the skill does and when to use it

The markdown content contains instructions, examples, and guidelines that Claude follows when the skill is active.

# Frontend Design

---
name: frontend-design
description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
---

## Ground your designs in the subject matter

If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.

Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.

Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
- Using all caps for labels.
- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.

Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.

Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique

For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.

All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

# Claude Code Skills: Comprehensive Summary

## Skill Locations

Skills load from these locations, with priority order when names conflict:

| Location | Path | Scope | Priority |
|----------|------|-------|----------|
| **Enterprise** | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` in managed settings directory | All users on deployed machines | 1 (highest) |
| **Personal** | `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | All projects on machine (not Cowork/cloud) | 2 |
| **Project** | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | Sessions in repository | 3 |
| **Nested** | `<subdir>/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | Sessions in/below subdirectory | Loads when Claude edits files there |
| **Additional directory** | `--add-dir` paths with `.claude/skills/` | Single session | Watched for live changes |
| **Plugin** | `<plugin>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | Wherever plugin is enabled | Namespaced as `/plugin-name:skill-name` |
| **claude.ai sync** | `~/.claude/skills/synced/` | Terminal sessions with sign-in, Cowork, cloud sessions | Short name if no conflict; full name as `/anthropic-skills:<name>` |

**Key discovery rules:**
- Project skills load from `.claude/skills/` in session start directory and all parent directories up to repo root
- Nested skills load on-demand when Claude edits files in that subdirectory
- In monorepos with conflicting names (root `deploy` + `apps/web/deploy`), both load; `/deploy` runs root skill, `/apps/web:deploy` runs nested skill
- Live change detection: Claude Code watches skill directories and picks up changes within the session (except bare mode)
- Run `/reload-skills` if you create a top-level skills directory after session start

## Essential Frontmatter Fields

All fields are optional; only `description` is recommended:

```yaml
---
name: my-skill                          # Command name (defaults to directory name)
description: What this does             # When Claude should use it (REQUIRED for auto-invocation)
when_to_use: Additional context         # Appended to description for matching
disable-model-invocation: true          # Only you can invoke; Claude cannot
user-invocable: false                   # Only Claude can invoke; hidden from `/` menu
allowed-tools: Bash(git *) Read Grep    # Pre-approve tools without permission prompts
disallowed-tools: AskUserQuestion       # Remove tools from Claude's pool while active
model: claude-3-5-sonnet                # Override session model for this skill
effort: high                            # Override effort level
context: fork                           # Run in isolated subagent context
agent: Explore                          # Which subagent type (with context: fork)
background: false                       # Wait for fork result (default: true)
argument-hint: "[issue-number]"         # Autocomplete hint
arguments: [issue, branch]              # Named positional args for $name substitution
paths: "src/**" "*.test.ts"             # Glob patterns; only auto-load for matching files
shell: bash                             # bash or powershell for !`command` injection
hooks:                                  # Register hooks when skill invokes
  - event: before-edit
    path: script.sh
metadata:                               # Free-form YAML for custom tooling
  entitlement: pro
---
```

**Frontmatter validation:**
- Boolean fields accept `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `1`, `0`, `true`, `false` (case-insensitive)
- If frontmatter YAML doesn't parse, skill still loads with empty metadata
- Run `claude plugin validate .claude/skills` to find malformed `SKILL.md` files

## Token & Context Behavior (Progressive Disclosure)

**Skill listing context cost:**
- Budget: 1% of model's context window
- Includes: skill name + description (truncated to 1,536 characters combined with `when_to_use`)
- When overflow: Claude Code drops descriptions starting with least-invoked skills
- Full skill content loads only when invoked

**Skill content lifecycle:**
- When invoked: content enters conversation as single message, **stays across later turns**
- Claude Code doesn't re-read file on subsequent turns—write guidance for whole task
- Re-invocation with identical rendered content: short note instead of duplicate
- Dynamic context changes (from `!` commands): full content appended again
- Auto-compaction: keeps first 5,000 tokens of each skill, combined 25,000-token budget

**After compaction:**
- Skill descriptions stay in listing
- Full invoked skill content re-attached after summary (older skills can drop if many invoked)
- Most recent skills prioritized when budget exhausted

**Size recommendations:**
- Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines
- Move detailed reference material to supporting files
- Each line is recurring token cost across all turns where skill is active

## Supported File Structure

```
my-skill/
├── SKILL.md                # Required; frontmatter + markdown
├── reference.md            # Loaded on-demand when referenced
├── examples.md             # Loaded on-demand
├── scripts/
│   ├── helper.sh          # Executable via !`command` injection
│   └── helper.py          # Executed, not loaded as text
└── .claude-plugin/        # Optional: turn skill dir into plugin
    └── plugin.json
```

Reference supporting files from `SKILL.md` so Claude knows what each contains:
```markdown
For complete API details, see [reference.md](reference.md)
For usage examples, see [examples.md](examples.md)
```

## Dynamic Context Injection

**Inline form** (`!`command``):
```markdown
## Current changes

!`git diff HEAD`

## Status

!`git status --short`
```

**Multi-line form** (` ```! `):
````markdown
## Environment
```!
node --version
git status --short
```
````

**How it works:**
- Commands run **before skill content reaches Claude**
- Output replaces placeholder in rendered content
- Not re-scanned for further placeholders
- Inline form recognized only when `!` starts line or follows whitespace
- Disabled globally: set `"disableSkillShellExecution": true` in settings
- In synced skills: `!` commands never run on your machine (v2.1.228+)

**Tool selection:**
- Default: Bash tool (merges stderr to stdout)
- `shell: powershell` with PowerShell tool enabled: runs via PowerShell
- `shell: bash` on Windows without Git Bash: invocation fails
- Timeout: 2 minutes per command
- Exit code 1 from search commands (grep, git diff, find) = normal result
- Other exit codes ≥1 = failure, aborts skill invocation

**Permission checks on injected commands:**
- Checked against permission rules before rendering
- Deny rule: aborts with "Shell command permission check failed"
- Pre-approve with `allowed-tools: Bash(git *)`
- In auto mode: unmatched commands load with instruction to Claude

## String Substitutions

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `$ARGUMENTS` | All passed arguments |
| `$0`, `$1`, `$ARGUMENTS[N]` | Argument by 0-based index |
| `$name` | Named argument (from `arguments` field) |
| `${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}` | Current session ID |
| `${CLAUDE_EFFORT}` | Current effort: low/medium/high/xhigh/max |
| `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` | Skill's directory (independent of cwd) |
| `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` | Project root |
| `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` | Plugin installation directory |
| `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` | Plugin persistent data directory |

**Examples:**
```yaml
---
name: fix-issue
description: Fix GitHub issue
arguments: [issue, branch]
allowed-tools: Bash(${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/*)
---

Fix issue $issue on branch $branch

Run: `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/fix.sh $0 $1`
```

**Escaping:** Use `\$1.00` to prevent expansion of literal `$` before digits/ARGUMENTS/named args

## Invocation Control

| Frontmatter | You invoke | Claude invokes | In context |
|-------------|-----------|----------------|-----------|
| (default) | ✓ via `/name` | ✓ auto + on Skill tool | Description always; full skill when invoked |
| `disable-model-invocation: true` | ✓ via `/name` | ✗ blocked | No description in context; full skill only when you invoke |
| `user-invocable: false` | ✗ hidden | ✓ auto + on Skill tool | Description always; full skill when invoked |

**Use cases:**
- `disable-model-invocation: true`: Workflows with side effects (/deploy, /commit)
- `user-invocable: false`: Background knowledge (legacy system context)

**Pre-approve tools:**
```yaml
allowed-tools: Bash(git add *) Bash(git commit *) Read Grep
```
- Grant clears after user sends next message
- Does not restrict availability; permission settings still apply

## Headless & Non-Interactive Mode Behavior

**`-p` flag (non-interactive), Agent SDK, cloud sessions:**
- Skills load from project `.claude/skills/`, enterprise, and plugin sources
- Personal `~/.claude/skills/` does NOT load (except synced from claude.ai)
- Forked skills (`context: fork`) with `background: true` still block until complete
- Skill descriptions in listing, full content on invocation
- Dynamic injection commands run normally

**Bare mode (`--bare`):**
- Live change detection disabled
- No file watching for skill changes

**`--add-dir` skill discovery:**
- Loads `.claude/skills/` from added directory
- Watched for live changes
- Requires `project` setting source (on by default)
- Restricted by `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` and `--safe-mode`

## Practical Examples

### Reference Skill (Always Loaded Description)
```yaml
---
name: api-conventions
description: API design patterns for this codebase
---

When writing API endpoints:
- Use RESTful naming conventions
- Return consistent error formats
- Include request validation
```

### Task Skill (Manual Invocation Only)
```yaml
---
name: deploy
description: Deploy to production
disable-model-invocation: true
context: fork
agent: Explore
---

Deploy the application:
1. Run the test suite
2. Build the application
3. Push to the deployment target
```

### Dynamic Context Skill
```yaml
---
name: summarize-changes
description: Summarizes uncommitted changes
---

## Current changes

!`git diff HEAD`

## Instructions

Summarize the changes in 2-3 bullet points, then list risks.
```

### Skill with Named Arguments
```yaml
---
name: migrate-component
description: Migrate a component between languages
arguments: [component, from, to]
---

Migrate the $component component from $from to $to.
Preserve all existing behavior and tests.
```

Invoke: `/migrate-component SearchBar JavaScript TypeScript`

---

## Key Takeaways

1. **Skill discovery is progressive:** Descriptions always load; full content only on invocation
2. **Location priority:** Enterprise > Personal > Project > Nested (with conflicts resolved)
3. **Token efficiency:** Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines; use supporting files for reference material
4. **Dynamic content:** Use `!`command`` to inject live data before Claude sees it
5. **Invocation control:** Use `disable-model-invocation: true` for manual-only tasks, `user-invocable: false` for background knowledge
6. **Headless mode:** Personal skills don't load in `-p` runs; project/enterprise/synced skills do
7. **Subagent forks:** `context: fork` isolates execution; `background: false` waits for result

# Web Application Testing Toolkit

## Frontmatter
- **Name:** webapp-testing
- **Description:** Toolkit for testing local web applications using Playwright
- **License:** Complete terms in LICENSE.txt

## Summary

This toolkit enables automated testing of local web applications through native Python Playwright scripts. The primary bundled resource is `scripts/with_server.py`, which manages server lifecycle—supporting single or multiple concurrent servers.

**Core Approach:**
The documentation recommends a decision tree starting with whether content is static HTML. For dynamic applications, the workflow involves starting servers via the helper script, then writing Playwright automation that performs reconnaissance (screenshots, DOM inspection) before executing targeted actions on discovered selectors.

**Key Principle:**
The toolkit emphasizes treating bundled scripts as "black boxes" by consulting `--help` documentation first rather than reading source code, preserving context window space for actual automation logic.

**Reference Materials:**
Three example scripts demonstrate element discovery, static HTML automation, and console logging capture.

# Agent Skills Summary

## Progressive Disclosure Levels

Agent Skills use a three-tier information architecture. The first level includes metadata (name and description) preloaded into the system prompt. The second level comprises the full `SKILL.md` content, loaded when Claude determines relevance. Additional bundled files represent the third level, discoverable only as needed. This design mirrors "a well-organized manual that starts with a table of contents, then specific chapters, and finally a detailed appendix."

## Token Efficiency

By implementing progressive disclosure, metadata remains lightweight at startup. Context loads dynamically only when relevant, preventing unnecessary token consumption. The system accommodates "effectively unbounded" skill content through filesystem and code execution tools.

## Bundled Files and Scripts

Skills can include supplementary files (like `reference.md` or `forms.md`) referenced from the core `SKILL.md`. Code scripts serve dual purposes: Claude can execute them directly or read them as documentation. This modular approach keeps core skills lean while enabling specialized functionality.

## Authoring Best Practices

Key recommendations include: start with evaluation by identifying capability gaps, structure for scale by splitting unwieldy content, think from Claude's perspective by monitoring real usage, and iterate collaboratively. The guidance emphasizes that "Claude will use these when deciding whether to trigger the skill"—making metadata clarity essential.

## Security Considerations

Install skills only from trusted sources. Thoroughly audit unfamiliar skills before deployment, examining file contents, code dependencies, and bundled resources. Pay particular attention to external network connections the skill might establish.

# Impeccable: Design Language for AI Coding Agents

## What It Is
Impeccable is a design skill that improves AI-generated frontend interfaces. It provides structured guidance, design vocabulary, and automated quality checks to help AI coding agents produce consistent, professional designs rather than repeating common patterns.

## Structure

**Core Components:**
- Single skill: `/impeccable <command> <target>`
- 24 specialized commands covering design workflows
- 61 deterministic detector rules (run locally, no API needed)
- Reference files: `PRODUCT.md` (product context), `DESIGN.md` (system specs)

**Key Commands:**
Initial setup (`init`), planning (`shape`, `critique`), building (`craft`), refinement (`polish`, `audit`), and specialized adjustments (`bolder`, `quieter`, `animate`, `colorize`, `typeset`, `layout`).

## Anti-Pattern Guidance
Impeccable explicitly warns against:
- Overused fonts and gray text on colored backgrounds
- Pure black/gray (recommends tinted neutrals)
- Excessive card nesting
- Dated easing effects like bounce/elastic

## Supported Tools
Works with Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, Codex, Gemini CLI, and others through skill installation or plugin integration.

## License
**Apache 2.0** — open source with permissive usage rights.

# Taste-Skill Summary

**Project Purpose**
Taste-Skill is a framework providing portable agent skills that improve AI-generated user interfaces by emphasizing sophisticated layout, typography, motion, and spacing—moving beyond generic templates.

**Skill Structure**
The repository contains multiple specialized skills organized in the `skills/` folder, installable via `npx skills add`. These include implementation skills (code generation) and image-generation skills (reference boards). Each skill targets specific design contexts, from general-purpose to specialized visual languages.

**Core Parameter System**
Three adjustable dials (1-10 scale) control output:
- **Design Variance**: Layout experimentation intensity (centered/clean vs. asymmetric/modern)
- **Motion Intensity**: Animation depth (hover effects vs. scroll/magnetic interactions)
- **Visual Density**: Information density per viewport (spacious vs. dense dashboards)

**Key Variants**
- Primary: `design-taste-frontend` (v2, substantially rewritten)
- Legacy: `design-taste-frontend-v1` for backward compatibility
- Specialized: `gpt-taste`, `soft-skill`, `minimalist-skill`, `brutalist-skill`
- Image generation: `imagegen-frontend-web`, `imagegen-frontend-mobile`, `brandkit`

**Technical Details**
Specific file sizes and line counts aren't provided in the documentation. The project uses MIT licensing and maintains a changelog documenting version changes.

**Community Support**
92k stars, 6.2k forks, active sponsorship from Kimi AI and Vercel's open-source program.

# Unsplash API Guideline Requirements

## Technical Requirements

**Hotlinking:** "All API uses must use the hotlinked image URLs returned by the API under the `photo.urls` properties." Images must be served from Unsplash's servers, not downloaded and rehosted.

**Download Tracking:** When users perform download-like actions (saving to a blog, setting as header), you're required to "send a request to the download endpoint returned under the `photo.links.download_location` property." This tracks engagement.

**Attribution:** Applications displaying Unsplash photos must credit Unsplash, the photographer, and link to their profile using specific UTM parameters: `?utm_source=your_app_name&utm_medium=referral`

**API Security:** Keep your Access and Secret Keys confidential, potentially using a proxy for client-side access.

## Usage Restrictions

**No Core Experience Replication:** Unofficial clients, wallpaper apps, and similar applications that mirror Unsplash's primary functionality are prohibited.

**No Commercial Resale:** "You cannot use the API to sell unaltered Unsplash photos directly or indirectly (prints, on products, etc.)"

**Quality Requirement:** The API supports "non-automated, high-quality, and authentic experiences" only.

**Rate Limiting:** "Too many requests too quickly will get your access turned off."

**No Registration Requirements:** Users shouldn't need developer accounts; implement a proxy solution instead.

## How It Works

The shadcn registry functions as a distribution system. Users can "use the `shadcn` CLI to run your own code registry" to share custom components, hooks, and configuration files across projects. The system operates through `registry.json` files that define available items.

Registry components can be used in standard projects—the system explicitly notes it's "not limited to React," supporting various frameworks and project structures through the CLI distribution mechanism.

I found comprehensive information on AI agent screenshot self-critique loops for UI generation. Here are the key findings:

## Self-QA Loop with Visual Feedback

A self-QA loop has an AI agent render, screenshot, and critique its own output before handing it to you. For agents that produce visual output — dashboards, web pages, formatted documents, PDFs — the agent renders the output, takes a screenshot of the rendered result, and then uses a vision-capable model to critique what it sees visually.

## Why Visual Feedback Matters

Structured text that looks correct in raw form can look broken when rendered, and by capturing and evaluating the visual output, not just the raw text, the loop catches a category of errors that text-only QA would miss entirely.

## Quality Improvement Through Iterations

Self-Refine demonstrated approximately 20% absolute improvement across seven tasks through 2–4 iterations. Research shows diminishing returns after the first few rounds, and excessive iteration can actually degrade output quality or increase costs without meaningful improvement, so clear stopping conditions should be set: a maximum iteration count, a quality threshold score, or a no-progress check.

## Implementation Approaches

Rendering the demo caught bugs that static checks missed, making screenshot review a required loop in the workflow, involving capturing before/after screenshots at mobile, tablet and desktop, plus a reduced-motion capture.

One approach involves wiring a headless browser into the agent's loop so it renders the page, screenshots it, and reads its own output before it's allowed to say "done."

# Unsplash License Summary

## What's Allowed

According to Unsplash, users may **"download, copy, modify, distribute, perform, and use images from Unsplash for free, including for commercial purposes, without permission"** from photographers or the platform.

Additionally, **"no permission needed"** and **"attribution is appreciated"** but not required.

## Restrictions

The license explicitly prohibits two things:

1. **Selling images**: **"Images cannot be sold without significant modification."**

2. **Service replication**: **"Compiling images from Unsplash to replicate a similar or competing service"** is not permitted.

## Regarding AI

The provided content does not address AI training, AI generation, or machine learning applications. No specific guidance on these uses appears in the license documentation shown.

# Pexels API Guidelines Summary

## Attribution Requirements

The API mandates **prominent linking back to Pexels**. You must display either a text link ("Photos provided by Pexels") or their logo. Additionally, you should "Always credit our photographers when possible (e.g. 'Photo by John Doe on Pexels' with a link to the photo page on Pexels)."

## Rate Limits

The default quota is restricted: **"200 requests per hour and 20,000 requests per month."** Higher limits are available—contact Pexels with examples demonstrating proper attribution practices.

## Prohibited Uses

You cannot "copy or replicate core functionality of Pexels (including making Pexels content available as a wallpaper app)." The terms also warn: **"Abuse of the Pexels API, including but not limited to attempting to work around the rate limit, will lead to termination of your API access."**

## Access Model

All Pexels content remains free to use. The service emphasizes that you're "welcome to use Pexels content for anything you'd like, as long as it is within our" stated guidelines—meaning compliance with attribution and usage restrictions is essential for continued access.

input.content:
# Raising output quality: Skills, asset library, and backend mechanisms

Status: research and plan only. No code was changed. Date: 2026-10-02. Target: Claude Code 2.1.287 in `nxeon-claudebox`.

## TL;DR

1. **Ship one first-party plugin, `nxeon`**, from a read-only library mount. Load it with `--plugin-dir /workspace/library/plugin` and add `--add-dir /workspace/library`. Both flags were tested in this container in `-p` mode. The plugin holds about 8 small skills. Each run then pays only for their descriptions: about 450 tokens, and almost all of that is billed as cache reads (about $0.0002 per API call on Opus). A full skill body loads only when Claude uses it, typically 1–3k tokens.
2. **Fix a real blocker first.** `edit` mode passes an `--allowedTools` list without `Skill`, and `ask` mode passes `--tools` without it. Skills are therefore unusable in those modes today. Add `Skill` to `EDIT_TOOLS` and `ASK_TOOLS` in `claudebox/lib/runs.js`.
3. **Add an offline asset library** at `data/library` mounted to `/workspace/library:ro`, about 350 MB with no photos or about 450 MB with a photo pack. It contains:
   - icons: Lucide, Tabler, Phosphor, Heroicons, and Simple Icons
   - about 40 self-hosted OFL fonts with curated pairings
   - CC0 illustrations: Open Peeps, Humaaans, and Open Doodles
   - about 12 style presets
   - a home-grown section library
   - 6 scaffolds

   A flat `catalog.tsv` and `catalog.json` let Claude find things with one `rg` call instead of browsing the web.
4. **Bake tooling into the image** so Claude stops reinstalling it every run:
   - `nx-shot` (Playwright with chromium-headless-shell; screenshots downscaled to a fixed token budget)
   - `nx-check` (axe-core, console errors, overflow at 390 px, external requests, broken links, HTML lint; compact text output)
   - `nx-font`, `nx-icon` and `nx-new`

   Evidence: in the existing `goonies-fanpage` project, Claude ran `npm i playwright && npx playwright install chromium && sudo npx playwright install-deps` in `/tmp/pw` over and over, and took 9 screenshots. It also hotlinked Google Fonts, which has a GDPR problem in the EU.
5. **Make quality gates server-side and free by default.** After each run that changed web files, the app calls a new claudebox `/v2/check`. It runs `nx-check` at zero LLM tokens and turns any failures into a `fix` suggestion chip. The vision design review is opt-in per project (`off`, `once`, or `auto`). It runs in a Sonnet subagent so screenshots never enter the main context. Cost is about 1.8k image tokens per pass.
6. **Add brand kits and style presets:**
   - `.nxeon/brand.json` and `.nxeon/brand.css` live in the project. One line in the system prompt applies them.
   - The new-project dialog gets one optional "Style" dropdown backed by 12 presets. This is the only UI addition in phase 1.
7. **Measure with `claude plugin eval`**, which is built into 2.1.287. Its `--ablation with-without` mode runs a no-plugin baseline arm automatically. Combine it with 12 benchmark prompts, `nx-check` scores (free), and a blind pairwise screenshot judgment (Haiku or Sonnet). A full A/B costs roughly $15–40 on Sonnet.

---

## 1. Findings: Claude Code skills (verified in this container)

### 1.1 Format and loading

- **Layout.** A skill is a directory `<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter, plus optional supporting files (`reference.md`, `scripts/`, `assets/`).
  - Frontmatter fields used by 2.1.287 (docs, plus strings found in the binary): `name`, `description` (needed for auto-invocation), `when_to_use` (appended to the description), `allowed-tools`, `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, `model`, `effort`, `context: fork`, `agent`, `paths` (globs: auto-load only for matching files), `arguments`, `hooks`, `metadata`.
  - Substitutions: `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`, `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, `$ARGUMENTS`.
  - Dynamic injection: a line like `` !`cmd` `` runs before the skill content reaches the model. This is useful for injecting `brand.json`.
- **Progressive disclosure** (Anthropic engineering blog):
  - Level 1 is name and description, always in context.
  - Level 2 is the SKILL.md body, loaded when invoked.
  - Level 3 is bundled files, read on demand. Scripts are executed rather than read, so they cost nothing.
- **Listing budget.** Read from the binary: `budget = contextWindow × 4 chars × skillListingBudgetFraction (default 0.01)`, which is **8,000 characters (about 2k tokens) for a 200k window**.
  - Each description is capped by `skillListingMaxDescChars` (default 1536).
  - The cap can be overridden with `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET` or in settings.
  - On overflow, descriptions are truncated and bundled skills are trimmed first.
- **Once invoked, a skill body stays in context for the rest of the session**, and is re-attached after compaction (first 5k tokens per skill, 25k total). Rule: keep SKILL.md under about 150 lines and push detail into reference files.

### 1.2 Discovery in `-p` mode (tested with `claude -p --output-format stream-json`, reading the `init` event)

| Source | Loaded in `-p`? | Name in listing |
|---|---|---|
| `<cwd>/.claude/skills/x/SKILL.md` (project) | yes | `x` |
| `~/.claude/skills/x` (personal) | **yes** in 2.1.287. The docs say it does not load in `-p`, so don't rely on it. | `x` |
| `--add-dir D` with `D/.claude/skills/x` | yes | `x` |
| `--plugin-dir P` with `P/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `P/skills/x` | yes | `nxeon:x` (namespaced) |
| Bundled skills (`deep-research`, `dataviz`, `run`, `verify`, `debug`, `code-review`, `simplify`, `batch`, `loop`, `claude-api`, …) | yes, 20 entries | — |
| The same bundled skills with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS=1` | trimmed to `design`, `doctor`, `plugin-authoring` | — |

Implications:
- Bundled skills already cost listing tokens on every run. Some of them push against the owner's token rules: `run` ("launch this project's app to see your change"), `verify`, and `deep-research`.
- Use `--settings '{"skillOverrides":{"run":"off","verify":"off","deep-research":"off","loop":"off","batch":"off","claude-api":"off","workflow-authoring":"off","fewer-permission-prompts":"off","update-config":"off"}}'`. Keep `dataviz`, which helps with dashboards, and `code-review` and `simplify`, which are user-invocable.
- Alternative: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS=1`, which removes all of them.
- **Recommended delivery: `--plugin-dir`.**
  - It gives a namespace (`nxeon:`), so no collision with bundled or project skills.
  - The same plugin can later carry `hooks/` and `agents/`.
  - `claude plugin details nxeon` reports its projected token cost.
  - `claude plugin eval` can A/B it.
- **Also pass `--add-dir /workspace/library`** so Read, Glob and Grep can reach the assets in every mode. Uploads already work this way.
- **Users' project skills** (`<project>/.claude/skills`) keep working automatically. This gives power users per-project skills with no extra UI.

### 1.3 Mode and tool gate (bug to fix)

`claudebox/lib/runs.js`:
- `EDIT_TOOLS` and `ASK_TOOLS` do not contain `Skill`.
- In `edit` mode (`acceptEdits` with an `--allowedTools` list and `--permission-prompts none`), a Skill call would be auto-denied.
- In `ask` mode, `--tools` removes it entirely.
- **Fix:** add `"Skill"` to both lists. Skills that need to write files are still limited by the mode's tool gate, so this is safe.

### 1.4 Base-context economics (from the `runs` table)

The 8 historical runs show about 35k tokens of base context per API call (system prompt, tools, and agents), and **about 95% of input is cache reads** (2.59M cache-read tokens against 96 uncached input tokens).

| Item | Tokens | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Base context per call | ~35k | — |

## 2. Findings: what makes generated UIs look professional

Synthesized from Anthropic's frontend-design skill, impeccable, taste-skill, Refactoring UI-style practice, and WCAG 2.2:

1. **Decide tokens before markup.** A design plan of 4–6 named hex colors, 1–2 typefaces with roles, a type scale, a spacing scale, radii, shadows, and a layout concept with an ASCII wireframe. Then check the plan against the brief ("would I produce this for any similar prompt?") and revise generic parts. Everything is expressed as CSS custom properties in `:root` (or Tailwind theme variables) and nothing is hard-coded afterwards.
2. **Type.**
   - One modular scale, for example 1.200 or 1.250 for apps and 1.333 or 1.5 for editorial heroes. Use `clamp()` for fluid display sizes.
   - Body 16–18 px, line-height 1.5–1.7 (serif slightly more). Measure under 75–80 characters.
   - Use a deliberate typeface, not the default Inter, Roboto or Arial. Two families at most, clearly distinct.
   - Avoid the generated-page tells:
     - a single accented word in the headline
     - all-caps eyebrow labels on every section
     - `A · B · C` meta strings
     - an arrow appended to every CTA
3. **Spacing.** A 4- or 8-point scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128). Section padding comes from the scale, never ad hoc. Consistent gaps through flex and grid `gap`. Watch selector specificity that cancels section padding (frontend-design note).
4. **Color.**
   - Tinted neutrals derived from the brand hue instead of pure gray or black. Define in OKLCH for even lightness steps.
   - One accent used sparingly.
   - Semantic tokens (`--surface`, `--text`, `--muted`, `--accent`, `--danger`).
   - Contrast of at least 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text and UI elements (WCAG AA).
   - Dark mode via token swap, not via a second stylesheet.
5. **Known AI-slop clusters to avoid unless the brief asks** (from frontend-design):
   - cream background with serif display and terracotta accent (`#F4F1EA` and `#D97757`)
   - near-black with a single acid-green accent
   - hairline-rule broadsheet layouts
   - the SaaS card kit: identical rounded cards, the same soft shadow everywhere, gradient washes
   - numbered 01/02/03 markers on content that isn't a sequence
   - fade-up on every section
6. **Hierarchy and layout.**
   - The hero opens with the subject's most characteristic thing, not "big stat plus gradient".
   - Vary section rhythm: full-bleed, split, dense grid, quote band.
   - Spend boldness in one place.
   - Containers are `min(1140px, 92vw)`-style. Mobile-first breakpoints, no horizontal scroll at 360–390 px.
7. **Motion.** One orchestrated moment, for example the page-load sequence or one reveal. Interaction feedback of 150–250 ms with ease-out. Always respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. No bounce or elastic.
8. **Imagery.**
   - Real or credible imagery with consistent treatment (same aspect ratios, same grading or duotone).
   - SVG icons from one family at one stroke width, inline.
   - Images get `width`, `height` and `loading="lazy"`, plus modern formats and `srcset`.
   - **No emoji as icons.**
9. **Copy.** Real, subject-specific copy. Plain verbs and sentence case. Every CTA names its action. Placeholder lorem ipsum is a quality failure.
10. **Quality floor.** Semantic landmarks, one `h1`, alt text, visible `:focus-visible`, labelled form controls, skip link, 44 px targets, `lang` and `meta viewport`, a favicon, OG tags, and no console errors.

**Design-review loops: cost and benefit**

- Image cost on Opus 5.5 (high-resolution tier) is ⌈w/28⌉ × ⌈h/28⌉ visual tokens:
  - 1280×800 viewport: 1,334 tokens
  - 390×844 mobile: 434 tokens
  - a full-page capture is capped at 4,784 tokens

  **Never send full-page shots; send two viewport JPEGs (about 1.8k tokens per pass).**
- Self-Refine-style loops gain most in the first 1–2 iterations. Returns diminish after that and quality can regress, so cap at **one critique-and-fix pass** by default.
- Do the critique in a **subagent** (`design-critic`, Sonnet, tools `Read` and `Bash(nx-shot*)`). The images and its reasoning stay in its context; the lead receives a 10-line report of prioritized fixes.

  | Mode | Extra cost on Opus lead | Use |
  |---|---|---|
  | One pass | ~$0.05–0.15 | default for "auto" |
  | Two passes | ~$0.3 | — |
  | Iterative | uncapped | never |

- Deterministic checks catch most real bugs at zero tokens: overflow, contrast, missing alt, console errors, broken links. Run them first and send pixels to a model only when the user asked for "polish", or the project has visual QA set to `once` or `auto`.

**Reference-driven design.** Presets (moodboards as data) give the model a concrete target and reduce rework turns. Store a preset as a about 40-line JSON:
- palette with roles
- font pair from the local catalog
- scale ratio, radius, shadow and density
- motion dial
- layout motifs
- explicit "don'ts"
- optionally a 600 px reference thumbnail (about 450 tokens) that the critic can compare against

**Section and component library.** A small home-grown library of about 30 well-designed sections in plain semantic HTML plus CSS that consumes only `var(--token)` values. It works for static sites and can be pasted into JSX. It beats copying generic Tailwind UI clones because it inherits brand tokens automatically. Sections: nav ×3, hero ×6, features ×4, gallery ×2, testimonial ×2, pricing ×2, FAQ, CTA ×2, footer ×3, contact form, timeline, stats, team, product card and grid, cart drawer, blog list and post. Use shadcn/ui (MIT) via the shadcn CLI for React apps and dashboards, with an offline registry JSON in the library.

## 3. Asset library spec

### 3.1 Principles

- Use only permissive licences: MIT, ISC, Apache-2.0, OFL-1.1, CC0. CC BY items only where attribution is generated automatically.
- **No runtime CDN.** Assets are copied into the project, so previews and deployed sites are self-contained. This also avoids the Google Fonts GDPR issue (LG München I, 3 O 17493/20, 2022).

### 3.5 Update script (`deploy/library-sync.sh`, run on the host or in a throwaway node container)

1. Pin versions in `deploy/library.lock.json`: npm package names and versions, plus git URLs and commits.
2. `npm pack` each package into a temp dir and extract only the needed files (SVGs; woff2 for latin and latin-ext; CSS).
3. Copy LICENSE and NOTICE files into `LICENSES/`.
4. Normalise SVGs: strip width and height, keep `viewBox`, `currentColor`. Run SVGO with a safe preset.
5. Generate `index.tsv` per area, `catalog.tsv` and `catalog.json`. Tags come from upstream metadata: Lucide `icons/*.json` tags, Tabler `tags.json`, Phosphor `catalog`.
6. Verify licence allowlist: refuse anything not in {MIT, ISC, Apache-2.0, OFL-1.1, CC0-1.0, 0BSD}, unless it is in an explicit exception list.
7. Swap atomically: build into `library.new/`, then `mv`. Running containers see the new tree through the bind mount.
8. Write `library/VERSION`.

Monthly cron or manual. Expect about 2 minutes and about 500 MB of transient download.

## 4. Backend mechanisms

### 4.1 Scaffold and template system

- Templates live in `library/templates/<id>/` with a `template.json` containing `{id, title, when, stack, previewCommand, strip, files}`.
  - `static-site`: index.html, `assets/{css,js,img,fonts}`, tokens.css, base.css, 404, favicon.svg, robots.txt
  - `static-multipage`
  - `vite-react-ts-tailwind`: Tailwind v4, `base` from `BASE_PATH`, ESLint and Prettier, Vitest, one smoke test
  - `astro-site`: content collections, `base` from env
  - `express-api`: zod validation, helmet, pino, an error envelope, `/health`, `.env.example`, Dockerfile, a node:test smoke test
  - `fullstack-vite-express-sqlite`: better-sqlite3 migrations
- `nx-new <id> [--name]` copies the template into the cwd (never overwriting files), substitutes `{{name}}`, `{{slug}}` and `{{base}}`, and prints a 5-line "next steps".
- The **project-creation API** gains an optional `template` field (the app copies it at creation time, at zero tokens). Mid-conversation, the `nxeon:scaffold` skill tells Claude to run `nx-new` instead of writing boilerplate.
- Each template ships a `CLAUDE.md` (about 20 lines) with its conventions. Claude Code auto-loads this per project. Examples: where tokens live, how to add a page, the test command, lint and format.

### 4.2 Brand kit (per project)

- Files:
  - `.nxeon/brand.json`: `{name, tagline, voice, palette:{role:hex}, fonts:{display,body}, radius, density, motion, logo:"assets/logo.svg", preset:"editorial-warm", dont:[...]}`
  - `.nxeon/brand.css`: generated `:root{--color-*, --font-*, --radius-*, --space-*}` plus `@font-face` (fonts copied into `assets/fonts`).
- Created by:
  - (a) the new-project dialog's optional Style preset and logo upload, or
  - (b) Claude itself on the first design pass. The `nxeon:brand-kit` skill writes these files after the design plan, so later turns stay consistent.
- One system-prompt line, added only when the file exists: `Brand kit: .nxeon/brand.json (+ brand.css) — use these tokens/fonts; don't invent new colors.` About 25 tokens.
- UI: a compact "Brand" panel in project settings (swatches, two font dropdowns from the catalog, logo, preset). It is not in the chat view.
- Optional `nx-brand extract <logo.svg|png>` derives a palette (k-means in the script) when a user uploads only a logo.

### 4.3 Quality gates (cheap first)

| Gate | Where it runs | Token cost | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nx-check` (static) | claudebox `/v2/check {projectSlug}`, called by the app after a run that changed `*.html`, `*.css`, `*.jsx` or `*.tsx` | **0** (the result goes to UI chips, not the model) | on |
| `nx-check --browser`: axe-core in headless Chromium against the preview URL, plus console errors, overflow at 390 px and 1280 px, and failed requests | same | 0 | on when a preview is running |
| Lighthouse (performance, SEO, best practices) | same, on demand ("Audit" chip) | 0 | manual |
| Design critique (vision) | `design-critic` subagent invoked by the lead when project `visualQA` is `once` or `auto`, or when the user says "polish" or "review design" | ~2–4k (Sonnet) plus fixes | off |
| Code review | existing `code-reviewer` subagent | as today | manual or on "ship" |

**Flow.** The run ends, the app calls `/v2/check`, and it gets JSON back:

```json
{"score": 0-100, "issues": [{"sev", "rule", "where", "fix"}]}
```

If high-severity issues exist, the server adds a suggestion chip of kind `fix`: "Fix 3 accessibility issues". Its prompt contains the compact issue list (at most 15 lines). The user decides whether to spend tokens on it, so there is no new UI surface. The score can show as a tiny badge on the preview tab.

`nx-check` output contract: at most 40 lines, each `SEV rule file:line|selector — fix hint`, then `PASS`/`FAIL` totals. Claude can also run it itself in `auto` mode before finishing (one line in the web-quality skill: "run `nx-check` once at the end of a build; fix high-severity items only").

### 4.4 Image changes (claudebox Dockerfile)

- `npm i -g playwright-core@1.63 axe-core @axe-core/playwright`, then `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium-headless-shell` into `/opt/ms-playwright` (`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`). Expect about +300 MB. Memory per run is about 200 MB, within the 4 GB limit and `shm_size` 256 MB.

- Mount: `./data/library:/workspace/library:ro`. Add `--add-dir /workspace/library` and `--plugin-dir /workspace/library/plugin` to the CLI args. Make both feature-flagged via env (`NXEON_LIBRARY_DIR`).
